Shahd was a kind girl, but she always walked around frowning, as if she were carrying something heavy on her shoulders.

Her friend Dana smiled at everyone she met, young or old.

In the morning they got on the bus, and Dana said to the driver with a smile, "Good morning, Uncle Jamil!"

Uncle Jamil smiled and said, "Good morning to you, my dear." But Shahd just sat down and did not look at him.

At school they passed Auntie Umm Sa'id, who had been cleaning the yard since dawn.

Dana said to her, "Jazakillahu khayran, Auntie — the yard looks lovely." Umm Sa'id lifted her head, and you could see the tiredness melting from her face.

Shahd said to Dana, "Why do you smile at everyone? You don't even know them."

Dana said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Your smile in your brother's face is a sadaqah for you.' And it's a sadaqah that doesn't cost me anything."

Shahd said, "A sadaqah? Without money?" Dana said, "Try it for just one day."

Shahd was quiet. She did not say yes, and she did not say no.

The next day Shahd got on the bus. She wanted to say good morning, but the words came out softly, and her smile was small.

Uncle Jamil said, "Good morning to you, Shahd! That's the first time I've seen you smile."

Then she passed Auntie Umm Sa'id and said to her, "As-salamu alaykum, Auntie." Umm Sa'id returned her salam happily and said, "Welcome, my dear!"

And Shahd felt something light in her chest.

At break time, a new girl was standing alone, not knowing anyone.

Shahd went over to her, smiled at her, and said, "Come and join us."

When Shahd got home, she told her mother, "Today I smiled five times — and five people smiled back at me."

Then she laughed and said, "And Dana does this every single day!"

From that day on, Uncle Jamil would say, "Now there are two smiles on my bus."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Your smile in your brother's face is a sadaqah for you."

📖 Narrated by At-Tirmidhi. This is a tale told as a parable; it did not happen to anyone in particular.
